slides.en: 9 pujo words English can't translate
That smell in the air before pujo: shiuli flowers, new clothes, dhunuchi smoke and the last of the rain.
Literally 'seeing the goddess'. Really: walking all night with your gang, pandal after pandal.
Hours of talk with no agenda, on the para steps, over endless cups of cha.
Your neighbourhood, your pujo, your people. Every para believes its pujo is the best.
'The gift of eyes': the moment the artist paints Maa's eyes and the idol comes alive.
Food offered to the goddess, then shared with everyone. No khichuri ever tastes this good.
Dancing with a smoking clay censer to the beat of the dhak. Balance, smoke, pure joy.
Victory, farewell, pronams, hugs and sweets, all in one word.
'It will happen again next year.' What we tell Maa, and each other, when it's over.

slides.en: Pujo, as a 90s Bengali kid
4 am. The radio. Mahalaya.
Five days, five new outfits. And new shoes that bit.
The pop of cap guns, all day long.
The pujo annual, and the smell of fresh pages.
Ashtami anjali. And a stolen glance.
Bijoya pronam, and a fistful of naru.
Which one was you? Comment the number and tag your childhood pujo gang.
